person.name: Joseph_Brant
person.summary: Thayendanegea, known as Joseph Brant, was a Mohawk military and political leader who allied with Britain during the American Revolution. He led Mohawk and Loyalist forces in the New York frontier war, then helped establish the Six Nations community on the Grand River in present-day Ontario.

portrait.caption: Stylized portrait based on a historical source image
portrait.creator: AI generated artwork

conclusion: Joseph Brant turned fluency across Mohawk and British worlds into a lifetime of leadership through war, exile, and diplomacy. His defining achievement was helping the Haudenosaunee endure dispossession by building a renewed community at Grand River.

events.date_note: Born during the Mohawks' hunting season; no exact day is recorded
events.title: Born in the Ohio Country
events.description: Thayendanegea, later known as Joseph Brant, was born in March 1743 along the Cuyahoga River in the Ohio Country, where Mohawk families from the Mohawk Valley hunted seasonally. In Mohawk matrilineal society, he belonged to his mother Margaret's Wolf Clan.

Ohio Country.explanation: An eighteenth-century frontier region west of the Appalachian Mountains, claimed by several colonial powers and Indigenous nations; much of it is now Ohio and nearby U.S. states.

events.title: Served in Seven Years' War
events.description: As a teenage Mohawk ally of Britain, Brant joined campaigns against the French in Canada, including expeditions to Fort Carillon, Fort Niagara, and Montreal. British authorities awarded him a silver medal for his service alongside other Indigenous warriors.

events.title: Attended Moor's Charity School
events.description: In 1761, Brant attended [[Moor's Indian Charity School|Moor's Indian Charity School]] in Connecticut, an institution founded by Eleazar Wheelock. He improved his English literacy and encountered Anglican religious instruction while retaining close ties to Mohawk life and British Indian Department networks.

Moor's Indian Charity School.explanation: An eighteenth-century Connecticut school founded by Eleazar Wheelock to educate Indigenous students; it was a predecessor institution to Dartmouth College.

events.title: Married Margaret
events.description: In 1765, Brant married Margaret, the daughter of a Virginia planter, in the Mohawk Valley. They had two children.

locations.name_modern: Mohawk Valley, New York, United States

events.title: Joined British Indian Department
events.description: In 1772, Brant became secretary and interpreter to Guy Johnson in the British Indian Department and received a captain’s commission. His command of Mohawk and English placed him in negotiations between the Crown and the [[Haudenosaunee Confederacy|Haudenosaunee Confederacy]].

locations.name_modern: Mohawk Valley, New York, United States

Haudenosaunee Confederacy.explanation: An alliance of six Indigenous nations—Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga, Seneca, and Tuscarora—also widely known as the Iroquois Confederacy.

events.title: Left for Canada and Britain
events.description: As revolutionary tensions overtook the Mohawk Valley, Brant left with Guy Johnson and Loyalist supporters for British-held Quebec. He later traveled to Britain to seek support for the Mohawk cause, returning to North America in July 1776.

locations.name_modern: Mohawk Valley, New York, United States

event_class.from_location: Mohawk Valley, Province of New York

events.title: Fought at Oriskany
events.description: Brant and Mohawk warriors fought in the British-allied force that ambushed a Patriot relief column near Fort Stanwix during the Battle of Oriskany. The battle brought Mohawk, Oneida, Seneca, and other [[Haudenosaunee|Haudenosaunee nations]] into direct conflict with one another.

images.caption: Fort Stanwix National Monument
images.creator: National Park Service Digital Image Archives

Haudenosaunee.explanation: An Indigenous confederacy also known as the Iroquois Confederacy or Six Nations, comprising nations including the Mohawk, Oneida, and Seneca.

events.title: Led frontier war raids
events.description: In 1778, Joseph Brant commanded Mohawk and Loyalist fighters known as Brant's Volunteers in raids on settlements across the New York frontier. His force took part in the attack on Cherry Valley, amid a brutal conflict in which civilians, soldiers, and Indigenous communities suffered heavily.

locations.name_historic: Cherry Valley, Province of New York
locations.name_modern: Cherry Valley, New York, United States

events.title: Published Mohawk prayer book
events.description: In 1780, at Fort Niagara, Joseph Brant helped prepare and publish an Anglican prayer book in the Mohawk language for Mohawk-speaking Christians displaced by the American Revolutionary War.

event_class.title: Book of Common Prayer in Mohawk
event_class.impact: It made Anglican devotional material available in Mohawk during the Revolutionary War.

events.date_note: The marriage occurred during the winter of 1779–1780
events.title: Married Catharine Croghan
events.description: During the winter of 1779–1780, at Niagara, Brant married Catharine Croghan, also known as Ahdohwahgeseon. Their marriage took place among Haudenosaunee refugees gathered around the British post after the destruction of their villages during the American Revolutionary War.

events.title: Settled the Grand River
events.description: After the loss of Mohawk homelands in New York, Brant led many Haudenosaunee families from the Niagara area to land set aside under the [[Haldimand Proclamation|Haldimand Proclamation]]. He helped organize the new Six Nations community on the Grand River.

locations.name_modern: Six Nations of the Grand River, Ontario, Canada

images.caption: 1821 survey of Grand River Indian lands
images.creator: Creator:Thomas Ridout

Haldimand Proclamation.explanation: A proclamation issued by Governor Frederick Haldimand on 25 October 1784 that set aside Grand River land for Mohawk people and other Six Nations people displaced by the American Revolution.

event_class.from_location: New York and British refugee settlements

events.title: Petitioned in London
events.description: In 1785, Joseph Brant traveled to London to petition the Crown for compensation, secure land tenure, and continued support for [[Haudenosaunee|Haudenosaunee]] settlers. He met King George III and other British officials to present Indigenous concerns directly.

images.caption: Joseph Brant portrait by George Romney, 1776
images.creator: George Romney

Haudenosaunee.explanation: A confederacy of Indigenous nations also widely known as the Iroquois Confederacy; Brant represented its displaced Loyalist communities after the American Revolution.

events.title: Met George Washington
events.description: In 1792, Joseph Brant traveled to Philadelphia and met President George Washington as disputes over Indigenous land and frontier warfare continued. He discussed peace and sought recognition of [[Haudenosaunee|Haudenosaunee]] interests while maintaining diplomatic ties with both British and American authorities.

Haudenosaunee.explanation: The Haudenosaunee, also called the Iroquois Confederacy, is a political alliance of Indigenous nations in northeastern North America.

events.title: Moved to Burlington Bay
events.description: Brant relocated with Catharine and their family from the Grand River to his estate near Burlington Bay. The household lived in a substantial residence, where Brant continued to receive visitors and conduct political correspondence.

locations.name_modern: Six Nations of the Grand River, Ontario, Canada

events.title: Death at Burlington Bay
events.description: Joseph Brant died at his home near Burlington Bay in Upper Canada on November 24, 1807, aged 64. He was buried at the Mohawk Chapel near Brantford.
